Work Personal Assistant

Adam's day-to-day School Tech work assistant in Cowork.
Cowork · Desktop workspace

What it is

A Cowork assistant that handles Adam's School Tech work and speaks in his own colleague voice. It is the work counterpart to the Personal Assistant — same style baseline, different scope. It is Adam-only: a staff-template rollout has been deferred with no date, so this brief describes a single-operator tool, not a template awaiting replication.

The design intent is stated in its own procedure files: it is a secretary, not a reporter. It takes work off the operator's memory, holds it in a structured store, and brings it back at known times. A task the operator has to remember to ask about is a task the system failed on.

What it does

Writing and correspondence

  • Rewrites work emails and messages to match Adam's tone, adapting register to the recipient — formal for vendors and leadership, casual for quick internal notes.
  • Drafts internal messages, vendor emails, customer follow-ups, and leadership updates.
  • Runs an always-on AI-tell cleaning pass on anything it writes, so drafts do not read as machine-generated.
  • Answers work questions directly, and searches the web when a question needs current information.
  • Summarizes work content — emails, docs, and threads Adam shares.

The daily agenda and the two standups

  • Produces the daily agenda on schedule or on demand, same layout either way: a Needs You Today lead card first and always expanded, an at-a-glance KPI strip second, then collapsed accordion sections for the detail. It triages before it renders, so the top of the page is what actually needs Adam.
  • Runs as a morning standup and an evening standup, each of which reads the task store and reports against it.

Task management

  • Holds Adam's work tasks in a single structured store and ingests them from conversation — "add a task", "put this on my list", "remind me to".
  • Displays them on request as a list, a table, or a chart, and answers scoping questions like "what can I knock out in 30 minutes".
  • Runs a nudge protocol across the two daily standups rather than waiting to be asked, and interrogates stalls — if an item is not moving, it asks why.
  • Updates and closes on Adam's word. It has explicit boundaries on what does not become a task.

Project tracking and meeting ingestion

  • Maintains the STA Project Tracker. The D1 tracker behind the hub's Projects tab is canonical for project state — projects, statuses, stages, open items, stage history, timelines — read and written only through the sta-tracker MCP tools.
  • Ingests the five recurring dev and support meetings, Granola first with Zoom as fallback, and accepts manually pasted transcripts.
  • Reads before it writes and reconciles on conflict. If a human changed the same field, it stops and reports rather than overwriting. Humans edit the same store through the hub tab, so conflicts are expected and never silently resolved.
  • Logs every ingested meeting so a meeting is never processed twice.

After-meeting checklist

  • Turns a customer meeting into a five-part wrap-up: the case comment, the Salesforce field list, Adam's own manual steps, the customer email, and what the customer owes back.
  • Works for any customer meeting type — implementation and migration, sales and discovery, support and escalation.
  • Hand-back only. It never writes to Salesforce.

Product support

  • Handles School Tech product troubleshooting, walks Skyward navigation click-paths, and works through remote-access and SQL Server diagnostics — capabilities absorbed from the retired STA Support Expert.
  • Extends to RMA workflows, support operations, the Salesforce Case schema, and implementation and migration questions.
  • Runs the Skyward weekly intelligence scan on demand and saves an HTML digest.

Records that build over time

  • Annual review prep. A year-long, append-only capture file organized by nine stable content buckets rather than by any review form's questions, so the year-end self-evaluation is written from a dated, sourced record instead of memory. Capture is silent and immediate.
  • Work brain capture. New work-context facts — a new vendor, a process detail, a colleague update — are written to Adam's Work Brain automatically, without asking.
  • Background logging. Three always-on silent behaviors: context-file maintenance, per-user enhancement logging, and central usage and feature-request capture. Any wish or friction Adam mentions in passing is captured.
  • Interaction rankings. A structured record of Adam's self-ratings on work interactions, taken before external feedback.
What the rankings capability is, stated honestly. Treat it as a structured record and an anti-anchoring discipline — not a demonstrated route to better self-judgment. A 2026-08-06 research commission found no evidence that self-rating before external feedback improves outcomes in a professional-conduct context, and self-versus-objective agreement for managerial competence sits at r = .04. The capability carries ten stop conditions, including one that suspends scoring after five consecutive scored deficits with no adverse outcome.

How it grounds an answer

  • Knowledge base first. A hard rule: it searches the KB before answering rather than reasoning from what it already carries.
  • Every claim that can go stale carries a date, and it uses four truth labels rather than a simple verified/unverified split.
  • It has a stated source precedence for when two sources disagree, so it resolves conflicts the same way every time instead of picking a winner per session.
  • It writes corrections back to the file that held the wrong answer, dated. Fixing a fact in chat alone would let the file reproduce the error next session.
  • No scoring without evidence. A valence gate governs any judgment it makes, and a deficit needs more evidence than a credit.

What it does not do

  • Never acts in external systems — and that is a written rule, not a platform limit. The Work Personal Assistant is the one agent holding the Gmail grant, so send_message, reply, forward, trash_message and trash_thread are all exposed to it and each executes the moment it is called. The Calendar tools create_event, update_event and delete_event are the same. What stops it is the "NEVER ACT in external systems" section of its own instructions, which names those tools. Verified 2026-08-20.
  • Never transcribes an inbound secret or auth code. If a one-time code, password, or token appears in something Adam shares, it stops rather than repeating it back.
  • Redacts student data on sight — a hard rule, applied without being asked.
  • Never writes to Salesforce. The after-meeting checklist hands back what to do; Adam does it.
  • Personal tasks — home, family, creative writing, personal finances → Personal Assistant.
  • Designing an agent or building a prompt → The Architect.
  • Sustained multi-source research → Deep Research.
  • Compliance interpretation or regulatory guidance → a security or compliance professional.

How to access it

It lives in Adam's Cowork workspace as a dedicated project. Cowork-only — there is no claude.ai Project version.

The one data rule. Never paste restricted data — student PII, HR records, financial details, or credentials. When in doubt, leave it out. The assistant redacts student data and refuses to transcribe credentials on its own, but that is a backstop, not a reason to paste it.
